question_text: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?

hint_ladder.title: Jeepney A: Bawat 12 min.
hint_ladder.text: Lista mo: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60... Mula 12, dagdag nang 12. Ito ang times ng jeep A.

hint_ladder.title: Jeepney B: Bawat 18 min.
hint_ladder.text: Lista mo: 18, 36, 54, 72... Mula 18, dagdag nang 18. Ito naman kay jeep B.

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang unang pareho.
hint_ladder.text: Tingnan kung aling numero ang lumabas sa parehong lista. Ang una ay 36. Yan ang LCM!

hint_ladder.title: Mental Trick: Jeep sabay sa 36.
hint_ladder.text: Tandaan: 'Jeepney 12 at 18, sabay sa 36!' Pagkatapos ng 36 min, sabay na ulit.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 24 is a multiple of 12, but it is not a multiple of 18, so it's not a common multiple.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 30 is the sum of 12+18, but LCM is about common multiples, not addition.

C.text: Correct. 36 is the smallest number divisible by both 12 and 18, making it the LCM.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 48 is a multiple of 12, but it is not a multiple of 18 and is larger than the LCM.

next_time_rule: **Key Takeaway:** LCM is the smallest common multiple. List multiples or use prime factors: 12=2²×3, 18=2×3² → LCM=2²×3²=36.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine commuting in Cubao: Jeepney A passes every 12 minutes, Jeepney B every 18 minutes. You just missed both. Kailan ulit sila magkasabay? That's the LCM!

The LCM is the smallest time both jeepneys will meet again. List their arrival times. Jeepney A at 12, 24, 36, 48, 60... Jeepney B at 18, 36, 54, 72...

Look for the first number that appears in both lists: 36. Ibig sabihin, after 36 minutes, sabay na naman silang dumarating. That's 36 minutes from now.

Verify: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 trips for A, 36 ÷ 18 = 2 trips for B. So in 36 minutes, Jeepney A completes 3 loops, B completes 2. Kaya LCM = 36. Mental Trick: "Jeepney 12 at 18, sabay sa 36!"
